text: Northstar Relay is an API traffic-routing service that shifts requests between healthy regions before a customer-visible outage develops. It evaluates endpoint health every ten seconds and applies a team's declared latency and error-budget rules without requiring application changes. In the frozen 30-day load test, the service routed 18.4 million synthetic requests and moved traffic in a median 42 seconds after a regional fault [EVD-001]. The same test kept 99.96 percent of requests within the declared availability target, compared with 99.71 percent for static DNS failover [EVD-002]. Reliability teams can use weighted routing for gradual migrations, health-triggered failover for incidents, and policy logs for post-incident review. These figures describe the controlled Northstar benchmark, not production performance for every workload. The product is designed for teams that need auditable routing decisions across multiple API regions while keeping their existing gateways and deployment workflow.
Additional API traffic routing notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Vector routing can help applications send requests to different places. Teams usually configure several regions and then choose rules that feel appropriate for their traffic. The dashboard offers settings for distance, health, and cost. There are many possible combinations, so operators should experiment before choosing one. This guide walks through the screens and describes the options, but the best configuration depends on the application and its users.
Additional vector routing notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

A latency budget is the maximum end-to-end response time a service can spend while still meeting a user-facing objective. Start with the product target, reserve time for the client and application, and give the remaining milliseconds to network routing and dependencies. Northstar's controlled checkout trace allocates 800 milliseconds end to end: 120 to the client, 280 to application work, 250 to dependencies, and 150 to routing variance [EVD-003]. During 240 injected delay events, a 150-millisecond routing allowance avoided unnecessary failovers while preserving the 800-millisecond target in 93 percent of traces [EVD-004]. Teams should calculate budgets by percentile, not average, because a mean can hide slow-tail failures. Revisit the allocation after architecture changes and keep the threshold paired with an error budget so that a fast but failing region is not treated as healthy. The example is a planning baseline, not a universal latency target.
Additional latency budgets notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Northstar Relay and Orbit Switch both route traffic across service regions, but they approach configuration in different ways. Northstar emphasizes explicit policies, while Orbit emphasizes automatic decisions. Buyers can compare dashboards, integrations, support plans, migration options, pricing models, and many other details. Northstar includes seven policy templates and several reporting views. Orbit may be a better fit for some organizations, while Northstar may be preferable for others. The right choice depends on team size, existing infrastructure, traffic patterns, risk tolerance, procurement rules, compliance needs, and how much control operators want during incidents. Customers should conduct a trial before deciding. A trial can include regional failure exercises, response-time observation, configuration review, and conversations with support. This page summarizes the products from Northstar's perspective and may not reflect every current Orbit feature. Product capabilities can change, packaging can change, and results vary across workloads. Teams should verify all claims during evaluation rather than relying only on a vendor comparison page.
Additional routing platform comparison notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Pricing is flexible for teams at different stages. Plans include useful routing features and support options, with room to grow over time. The starter plan begins at 480 credits per month, and larger deployments can contact the sales team. Actual charges depend on usage, regions, retention, and support. Talk with us to explore the package that makes sense for your organization.
Additional pricing notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Northstar Relay protects routing policy changes with scoped roles, signed audit events, and customer-managed approval rules. Every production policy edit records the actor, previous value, new value, timestamp, and approval state. The August control test covered 2,400 synthetic policy changes; all 2,400 produced a complete audit event, and 600 high-impact changes were held until a second approver acted [EVD-005]. Encryption is applied in transit and at rest according to the control inventory [EVD-006]. Customers can set log retention from 30 to 365 days and export events to their own monitoring account. Northstar personnel cannot bypass a customer's two-person approval rule through the application interface. These statements describe product controls, not a guarantee that a customer's deployment is compliant. Teams remain responsible for role assignment, export monitoring, and review of their own regulatory requirements. A current control summary and test boundary are recorded in the evidence register.
Additional security controls notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

The quickstart connects one test endpoint to Northstar Relay and sends a routed request from a local client. Create a workspace, add the endpoint, copy the generated example identifier, and run the sample command. A successful response includes the selected region and a policy-event identifier. Most sandbox workspaces finish the sequence in under ten minutes, although account review can add time [EVD-007]. The example uses a disposable local value and the sandbox hostname. Do not substitute production secrets or a live customer endpoint while learning the flow. After the request succeeds, open the event view to confirm which health and latency rules were evaluated. The quickstart proves basic connectivity only; it does not validate failover behavior, production capacity, or a complete security configuration.
Additional quickstart notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

A safe retry policy repeats only requests that are idempotent or protected by an idempotency key. Northstar returns a retryable marker for temporary routing failures and a non-retryable marker for policy or validation errors. The client test matrix uses exponential delays of 200, 400, and 800 milliseconds with random jitter, then stops after the third retry [EVD-008]. In 1,000 injected temporary failures, this policy recovered 941 requests without producing a duplicate write. The remaining 59 requests surfaced the final error to the caller. Do not retry authentication failures or malformed requests, because another attempt cannot repair them. For write operations, reuse the same idempotency key across attempts and retain it long enough for the server's deduplication window. The example values are defaults for the sandbox workload; production clients should set a total retry budget that remains inside their user-facing latency objective.
Additional API retries notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Lumina Labs used Northstar Relay during a staged migration between two fictional regions. Its engineering team reported that the routing policy reduced manual incident steps from nine to four and cut the median exercise recovery time from eleven minutes to six minutes across six drills [EVD-009]. The team kept its existing gateway and added policy-event exports to the incident channel. The account involved 14 services, but only five were included in every drill, so the results should not be generalized to the whole platform. Lumina also changed its runbook during the same period, which means the recovery improvement cannot be attributed to routing software alone. The case shows how auditable policies can support a migration; it does not prove a guaranteed time saving for other organizations.
Additional customer reliability story notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Northstar's 2026 routing benchmark compares health-triggered policies with static DNS failover under the same synthetic workload. Across 360 injected regional faults, policy routing restored a healthy path in a median 42 seconds, while static failover took 118 seconds [EVD-010]. The 95th-percentile times were 71 and 204 seconds respectively. Both configurations used three regions, identical health probes, and 18.4 million generated requests over 30 days. The benchmark excludes application cold starts and internet-wide resolver variation, so it isolates the routing layer rather than predicting complete incident recovery. Twelve fault runs were removed before analysis because the workload generator stopped early; the exclusion rule was defined in the test plan [EVD-011]. These results support a narrower claim: under the recorded laboratory conditions, health-triggered routing reacted faster than the static configuration. Teams should reproduce the test with their own latency objectives, dependency behavior, and change controls before using the figures for capacity or procurement decisions.
Additional routing benchmark notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

The NovaQueue integration connects queue health to routing decisions. It can be configured from the integrations screen and offers several useful options for operations teams. After setup, events appear in Northstar views and can help people understand what is happening. Different deployments may choose different settings. Review the fields carefully, test the behavior, and contact support if anything is unclear. The integration page includes screenshots and a general overview, while the full catalog contains details about other connectors.
Additional queue integration notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.

Northstar Relay is built by a small group of engineers who care about reliable systems. The company began after its founders encountered difficult regional incidents and wanted clearer routing decisions. Today the team works on policy controls, integrations, and operator tooling. Customers include software groups with a range of architectures. This page introduces the company's purpose and values, but it does not provide biographies, role histories, or links that establish the people behind the product.
Additional company background notes summarize navigation links, related settings, and support options without adding independently sourced claims.
